commitResults.messageBody:
Aigis uses task objects but the Java sources are in the default package and mix formatting, naming, and resource-handling conventions.

Move Aigis and Task into the aigis package. Rename the task collection and completion setter, centralize display constants, document public APIs, guard against a full task list, and update the launch path in the README.

The refactor aligns the application with the project Java standard and keeps task state changes and command output consistent.

Java changes need a project-local standard so future edits use consistent conventions.

Add the SE-EDU-based Java skill and make its files trackable in the repository.

The shared guidance gives future agents a repeatable review checklist for package structure, naming, formatting, and public API documentation.

Commit and branch naming need project-local guidance so repository history stays consistent.

Add the SE-EDU-based Git skill covering imperative subjects, line limits, WHAT/WHY bodies, and kebab-case branch names.

The shared checklist helps future agents prepare reviewable commits without authorizing commits or pushes by itself.

Future Java and Git work needs explicit project guidance so agents apply the same conventions.

Require the project Java and Git skills for source changes, commits, and branch names while preserving the explicit permission requirement for committing and pushing.

Centralizing these requirements in AGENTS.md makes them apply consistently across repository tasks.

Claude-based repository work needs the same project guidance as other agents.\n\nReference the Java and Git standard skills from CLAUDE.md so coding, commit, and branch conventions remain consistent across agent entry points.

Todo commands need a concrete task subtype so their status and list output are distinct from other task kinds.

Implement Todo as a Task subclass and prefix its display with the todo marker.

Deadline commands need to retain both task descriptions and due dates while using the common Task status behavior.

Implement Deadline as a Task subclass and include its due date in the display representation.

Event commands need to retain their start and end times while participating in the common Task lifecycle.

Implement Event as a Task subclass and include both event times in its display representation.

Aigis must construct the appropriate subtype for each task command and reject incomplete structured input without crashing.

Route todo, deadline, and event commands to their subclasses, trim parsed fields, and validate required delimiters before calling substring.

Aigis command changes need repeatable console checks that capture complete sessions and preserve exact output formatting.

Add the test-ui skill, its Java 25 runner, and a plan covering task lifecycle, structured tasks, invalid numbers, and malformed commands.

The command loop combined input handling, parsing, validation, and task
updates in one long method. This made the happy path harder to follow
and repeated parsing details across branches.

Extract command-processing helpers and name command markers and usage
messages. Keep each helper at one abstraction level so parsing and task
updates are easier to understand and maintain.

Task descriptions and completion state are implementation details, but
protected fields expose them directly to every subclass. This weakens
the class boundary and allows accidental changes.

Make the fields private while keeping all state access through the
existing constructor, getter, setter, and display methods.

Unrecognized input previously fell through the dispatcher without
feedback. This made the final branch ambiguous and left users unable to
tell whether their command was accepted.

Print an explicit fallback response and add a UI regression case
confirming that unknown commands do not create tasks.

Task construction currently accepts null and blank fields, allowing invalid state to enter the task model. Add a shared validation function and apply it to task descriptions, deadlines, and event times so invalid values fail consistently before storage.

Task constructors now reject invalid fields, but the command loop must keep running when user input triggers those failures. Catch construction exceptions before storing tasks and add interleaved UI cases that verify rejected inputs do not corrupt task counts or completion state.

The source tree keeps the application entry point and task domain classes in one package, which limits separation as the project grows. Move Task, Todo, Deadline, and Event into aigis.task, update Aigis imports, and keep src/main/java as the source root so package paths remain aligned.

commitResults.messageBody:
# Conflicts:
#	src/main/java/aigis/Aigis.java

Aigis currently owns the mutable task collection directly, so command processing is coupled to the collection implementation. Extract the collection boundary to make task ownership explicit and prepare the remaining responsibilities for later extraction.

- Centralize task capacity checks in TaskList.
- Keep indexed access, addition, removal, and persistence conversion together.
- Preserve all existing command output and storage behavior.

Aigis currently owns the console scanner, startup and closing text, and every output call, which couples command processing to the command line. Move those interactions behind Ui so the application logic can be tested and reused without depending on console details.

- Let Ui manage console input and lifecycle.
- Move banners, task-list display, and messages into Ui.
- Keep command recognition and task mutations in Aigis for the next extraction.

Aigis currently mixes command syntax recognition, task construction, and command execution, which makes the main loop responsible for several unrelated concerns. Introduce a typed parser result so input interpretation has a clear boundary before execution.

- Move command prefixes, markers, validation, and task construction into Parser.
- Return typed commands containing task numbers, tasks, or response messages.
- Keep execution, task state changes, persistence, and console presentation outside Parser.

Storage was a static utility tied to the default data file, which made
its persistence dependency implicit and prevented alternate file locations.

Give Storage a configured file path and inject one instance into Aigis for
both loading and saving. Resolve the path once and preserve the existing
serialization, atomic save, and malformed-record handling behavior.

Aigis still had to allocate arrays and translate the loaded count into a
TaskList, coupling the application flow to Storage's persistence details.

Make Storage load and save TaskList objects directly, and remove the
obsolete array conversion and loading constructor. Keep task capacity,
record parsing, malformed-record handling, and file serialization unchanged
while giving each class a clearer domain-level boundary.

Aigis previously assembled all dependencies and ran the command loop inside
main, which made the application lifecycle difficult to reuse or test as an
object.

Give Aigis explicit Ui, Storage, Parser, and TaskList fields with a
constructor and run method. Keep main as a thin default-path launcher and
let Aigis own console cleanup through AutoCloseable.

Parser accepted a second deadline /by or event /to marker as ordinary
field text, creating malformed tasks instead of reporting invalid input.

Reject repeated /by, /from, and /to markers before task construction. This
keeps the existing usage messages and prevents ambiguous command fields from
being persisted.

Aigis previously used a central switch to interpret parsed command data and
mutate the task list, so adding commands required editing the coordinator.

Introduce an abstract Command with concrete exit, list, add, delete,
mark, unmark, and message commands. Make Parser construct these commands
and reduce Aigis to parsing, executing, and checking isExit while preserving
all existing UI and persistence behavior.

WHAT: Add AigisException for recoverable command failures, route parser and validation errors through the application loop, and add Ui.showError for user-facing presentation.

WHY: Commands should report failures consistently while Aigis remains responsible for coordinating execution and UI behavior.

The existing console messages are preserved, including the full-list precedence for add commands.

WHAT: Add Ui.showLine and render a divider before and after every command. Update the UI test plan with the new exact transcripts.\n\nWHY: Match the stretch-goal command loop while keeping command cleanup in a finally block, including when the user exits or a command reports an error.

WHAT: Parse deadline inputs as LocalDate values, display them as MMM dd yyyy, and serialize them in ISO format for storage. Reject non-ISO dates and skip malformed saved deadline records.\n\nWHY: Date values should be represented semantically in task objects so validation, display, and persistence use a consistent format.
WHAT: Add a UI test for a valid leap day and invalid calendar dates.\n\nWHY: Verify that LocalDate accepts real leap days while rejecting impossible dates and months at the command boundary.

WHAT: Add a shared DateFormats utility and use it from Parser and Deadline.\n\nWHY: Keep the ISO input format and display format defined in one place so deadline parsing and rendering cannot drift apart.

WHAT: Add support for searching task descriptions with find x.

WHY: Let users quickly locate tasks without scanning the complete task list.

WHAT: Add Javadocs to non-private methods in the task subclasses.

WHY: Keep the public and protected Java APIs consistently documented for
readability and maintenance.

WHAT: Replace the starter README with a GitHub-flavored guide for Aigis.

WHY: Give users clear setup instructions and an organized reference for
all supported chatbot commands.
